title: P09.11: finite JSON decoder PHPDoc correction with numeric-key preservation
context: P09.11 baseline-free diagnostics expose inaccurate JSON decoder PHPDoc: associative json_decode converts integer-looking JSON member names to PHP integer keys; non-list objects may mix string/integer keys. Preserve all currently accepted decoded values, including numeric names, rather than reject or discard them for typing.
decision: Finite PHPDoc-only delta: JsonCanonical::decode return becomes array<array-key, mixed>|string|int|float|bool|null; JsonCanonical::decodeObject return becomes array<array-key, mixed>|null. SchemaBudget::admit schema parameter PHPDoc becomes array<array-key, mixed> because JSON object names may be numeric and recursive schema arrays include lists. These exact three PHPDoc fields change. Native signatures and runtime accepted JSON values remain unchanged; named consumers validate their own map boundaries. Record exact two manifest fields, package CHANGELOG and public API projection. Feature-owned Internal SQL adapters may add only four new Golden class surfaces; regenerate precise inventory delta without resetting BC/schema baselines or approvals. Malformed SQL/worker/protocol values fail explicitly, valid SQL/JSON behavior and established scope/value-comparison semantics remain covered by existing lanes and focused regression cases.
rationale: Accurate public type documentation must follow PHP runtime key behavior; D120 prohibits invented PHPDoc narrowing or suppression. This is a declared finite repository correction under B6, D17 and D125, not an undeclared behavior or native API rewrite.

evidence.note: Original decoder return.type diagnostics and existing source.
